question: The Dampier-Hodges line is related to which of the following?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Sundarban’s**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points:__**

__
 
• The British developed the **Dampier**-**Hodges **Line in **1828**.
 
• It is a hypothetical line that runs through West Bengal's** 24 Parganas North and South districts.**
 
• It is regarded as the northern limit of the **Indian Sundarbans**, which contain both forested and heavily inhabited areas.
 
• In Bangladesh, only forested regions are regarded as being a part of the **Sunderbans**, despite the fact that a 20 Km buffer zone known as the **Sunderban Impact Zone **and an **Ecologically Critical Area **have been **designated**.
 
• The Indian Sundarbans, which are thought to be located south of the **Dampier Hodges line**, have an area of **9,630 square kilometres**, of which **4,263 square kilometres **are **mangrove forests. **

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information:__**

 
• **Andaman and Nicobar Islands:**

 
 
• **​**At the confluence of the** Bay of Bengal** and the **Andaman Sea **are the **Andaman **and **Nicobar Islands**, a union territory of India made up of **572 islands**, **37 **of which are **inhabited**.
 
• The **Andaman Sea **divides the region from **Thailand **and **Myanmar**, and it is located roughly 150 km (93 mi) **north **of **Aceh **in **Indonesia**.
 
 
 
• **Bay of Cambay: **
 
 
• **​**The **Gulf of Khambhat**, formerly known as the **Gulf of Cambay,** is a bay that borders the **Gujarat state **just north of **Mumbai **and **Diu Island **on the Indian** Arabian Sea coast.**
 
• In the north, the Gulf of Khambhat is only around **20 kilometres** (12 miles) broad, whereas in the south, it can be as large as **70 kilometres **(43 miles).
 
 
 
• **Palk Strait: **
 
 
• **​**The **Jaffna District **of Sri Lanka's Northern Province and the Indian state of Tamil Nadu are separated by the **Palk Strait.**
 
• It links Palk Bay in southwest with the **Bay of Bengal** in **northeast**.
 
 

ee:T
